It also periodically forgets all of your tickets locally and needs to resync from the network. It doesn't matter if you were just looking at the ticket three minutes ago. godwinson__4-8 · Nov 14, 2026

No government service should require a frontend.

API only access where a frontend is currently available should be a legal requirement. For one thing, not doing so is prejudicial regarding accessibility.

I really yearn for a world where we stop making people deal with all these garbage frontends. Especially in the coming age of personal LLMs on device - anyone should be able to create their own frontend for any service and drive their own version specifically tuned to them. Make the standard frontend as simple and accessible as possible (minimal scripting - I think you could have a government agency set this as a regulatory limit in terms of KB of JavaScript) and just cut the fat and the abhorrent waste.

Clients will ship with defaults. Most people's personal tunes will not deviate much from each other at all. But people who actually care can make it as interesting as they want. Instead what we have now is a system that incentivizes people to make the default too interesting to justify their own employment. It's rare to come across a frontend these days that doesn't scream absolute garbage.
